Method of Attack: Leveraging unpatched Microsoft Exchange server vulnerabilities (ProxyLogon) to breach enterprise network
Use of PowerShell scripts to kill security tools, delete shadow copies, steal SAM file, delete event logs, disable Windows Defender, uninstall security tools, expand permissions
Deployment via RDP and Windows Management Instrumentation (WMI) to install software and run scripts
Use of commercial remote desktop utility (Remote Utilities) and Tor Browser to maintain access
File encryption appending suffix '.epsilonred' to targeted files and folders
Dropping ransom note modeled after REvil ransomware
Attack Vector: Exploitation of Microsoft Exchange ProxyLogon vulnerabilities
Indicators of Compromise: Presence of PowerShell scripts numbered 1-12 and named scripts like c.ps1 (clone of Copy-VSS)
Ransom note with instructions similar to REvil ransom note
File suffix '.epsilonred' appended to encrypted files
Payment of ransom: 4.28 BTC (~$210,000) on May 15
